meta.title: Toledo Metro K-12 STEM Camp Finder
meta.region: Toledo, Ohio metro (Lucas County + Sylvania, Maumee, Perrysburg, Bowling Green, Oregon, Holland, Waterville)
meta.note: Data compiled from adversarially-verified deep research. Verify dates and contacts before registering — programs change annually.

providers.name: Bowling Green State University
providers.description: Largest anchor: 30+ Pre-K–12 summer camps and workshops including AI-assisted cybersecurity (CyberGuardians), advanced manufacturing, forensic science, marine biology and health-career camps. 2026 registration closed; 2027 applications open around Dec 1, 2026.

contact.namedContact: Kari Wilson, Coordinator of Pre-College Programs

providers.cost: Varies; camperships available (Rossford students may receive full tuition)

events.name: Advanced Manufacturing Camp
events.focus: Robotics/electronics, 3D printing & CAD, glass manufacturing (DLP printing, sintering); lunch, snacks and a take-home robot included

events.name: CyberGuardians Camp
events.focus: AI-assisted ethical hacking, network security, cybersecurity awareness, digital forensics
events.format: Day camp, 5 days — 2026 week not re-confirmed; verify with BGSU

providers.name: University of Toledo — Herb Innovation Center
providers.description: ~Two dozen summer camps including a middle-school AI/Data/Media Literacy camp and a high-school Engineering camp.

events.name: Hands-On AI, Data & Media Literacy Camp
events.focus: AI fundamentals, data literacy, algorithms, media authenticity
events.cost: $200; $25 for Ohio Council of Community Schools students ($175 scholarship)

providers.name: University of Toledo College of Engineering — K-12 Outreach
providers.description: Year-round K-12 engineering outreach. The Robotic Rubik's Cube Challenge sets up school Mechatronics Clubs (with Dana, Owens Community College and Toledo Public Schools, NSF-funded) with twice-weekly after-school training in electronics, coding and robotics; clubs start each September, including September 2026. Also runs the Introduce a Girl to Engineering series and the PEER high-school research program.

contact.namedContact: Robotic Rubik's Cube Challenge details at hybridplc.org

providers.cost: Varies; scholarships to UToledo and Owens available for participants
providers.season: School year — Mechatronics Clubs start each September

events.name: Introduce a Girl to Engineering Day
events.focus: Hands-on engineering exploration; from 2026 open to all middle school students

events.name: Introduce a Girl to Engineering Day (spring session)
events.focus: Hands-on engineering exploration; from 2026 open to all middle school students

providers.name: Owens Community College / Kool Kat Science
providers.description: Week-long STEM camps run by Kool Kat Science through Owens' Workforce & Community Services: Inspector Elle mystery/forensics and LEGO robotics (ages 6–8), Micro:bit electronics & coding and Tinkercad/3D printing (ages 8–12). Kool Kat has also announced Future Builders Lab, a 15-week grades 3–6 afterschool program with New Leaf Group launching fall 2026 (confirm directly).

location.venue: Owens Workforce & Community Services, 30335 Oregon Rd

contact.namedContact: Register through Owens Workforce & Community Services

providers.name: Imagination Station
providers.description: Downtown science center running week-long summer STEM camps for ages 6–13, plus a sensory-friendly week.

events.name: I.S. Fashion Week
events.focus: Science of materials, design and making

events.name: Sensory Friendly Camp: Best of the Summer

providers.name: Toledo Zoo & Aquarium
providers.description: Summer Safari Camp (single-day, half-day and full-week options) and a Spring Break Camp for a Day, with STEM tracks: Zoo Animal Rescue, Radical Reptiles, Junior Zookeeper, Wild Art and conservation field camps. Each camper gets two t-shirts, a water bottle and daily snack.
providers.cost: Varies; member pricing on every camp. Before care $30/wk (8–9am), after care $60/wk (3–5pm)

events.name: Spring Break Camp for a Day
events.focus: Animal behavior, jr. zookeeper, ornithology, aquatic science, creative STEM

events.name: Summer Safari Camp (e.g. Zoo Animal Rescue)

providers.name: Challenger Learning Center (ESC of Lake Erie West)
providers.description: NASA-style space-station/mission-control simulations where students work as scientists and engineers on a space mission. Summer camps remain PAUSED for 2026 and resume summer 2027 — registration is expected to open early January 2027.

location.venue: 4955 Seaman Rd (simulation site); ESC at 2275 Collingwood Blvd

providers.name: YMCA of Greater Toledo
providers.description: Y Summer Adventure (school-age care with STEM-based programming, weekly field trips, an outdoor education day at the Sylvania YMCA/JCC and swimming), plus specialty camps including LEGO, and YMCA Storer Camps for ages 7–17.

contact.namedContact: Branch locations have their own numbers

providers.name: Toledo Minds

providers.description: FREE makerspaces (3D printers, Cricut, vinyl), plus Rookie Robotics and the 16-week STEM in the Stacks afterschool series (engineering, Scratch coding, microcontroller robotics) run with Kool Kat Science.

events.name: Rookie Robotics 2026 Series

providers.name: Snapology of Toledo-West
providers.description: STEM/STEAM camps and workshops for ages 4–14 using LEGO bricks, K'Nex and technology — robotics, coding, animation, preschool STEAM and competition teams. Camps also run during school breaks, not just summer.
providers.cost: Half-day camps from $149/week; one-day workshops from $29

providers.name: Bricks 4 Kidz Toledo
providers.description: LEGO-based STEM/STEAM camps, robotics & coding for ages 5–13. NOTE: the camps page currently returns no scheduled classes, and the listed phone and contact name could not be re-confirmed on the official page.

providers.description: STEM Camps for elementary through early high school across three metro centers.

providers.name: Penta Career Center
providers.description: VEX Robotics and STEM camps for students from Penta's 16 member districts. The June 2026 STEM camps drew a record 550 students in grades 3–9 across art, business, construction, criminal justice, culinary, forensics, welding, geology, health science and math.

providers.name: Camp Invention (National Inventors Hall of Fame)
providers.description: Hands-on K–6 STEM day camp. The 2026 program, 'Spark', has four themed experiences: The Infringers, Fur-ensics, Make Waves and Space Morphers. Hosted in local schools — find Toledo-area sites by ZIP.

providers.name: Toledo Technology Academy — TechFusion
providers.description: FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC) team. NOTE: the school's team page has not been updated in several seasons — contact the school for current team status.

providers.name: Ohio FIRST
providers.description: Statewide FIRST coordination — entry point for finding or starting a team. FIRST Robotics Competition (high school), FIRST Tech Challenge (grades 7–12) and FIRST LEGO League (ages 4–16). Ohio hosts the Miami Valley and Buckeye Regionals.

providers.name: Toledo Museum of Art
providers.description: Children's classes (ages 3–13) and teen classes (ages 14–18) in drawing, sculpture, mixed media, painting and portfolio development — STEAM creative skills. Summer, fall, winter and spring sessions; need-based scholarships cover 100% of tuition for most classes.

providers.name: National Museum of the Great Lakes
providers.description: Capt. Scupper's Kid's Club — recurring Saturday environmental-science and engineering sessions in the Great Lakes Community Education Center for ages 13 and under (all families welcome; children must be accompanied by a parent or guardian).
providers.cost: Free with museum admission; free for members and Museums for All

providers.name: Sylvania STEM Center
providers.description: Grassroots 501(c)(3) in a 2,600 sq ft facility: competitive FIRST robotics (grades 1–12, incl. FIRST LEGO League), programming clinics and STEM summer camps. Teams of ~8 meet twice weekly. NOTE: the website did not respond to automated checks and the founder's name could not be confirmed — verify directly before contacting.

contact.namedContact: Founder name NOT confirmed — sources disagree; verify directly

providers.name: EmpoweredAI — Young Empowered Authors
providers.description: FREE program where kids use AI tools to write and publish their own books on Amazon, covering narrative structure, worldbuilding and AI literacy. Signature 'Publishers Party' showcase. 120+ published authors and 35 titles in circulation to date; every participant is fully scholarshipped.

location.venue: Toledo (Art Tatum Zone / City of Toledo partners)
